mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered periods, or the effect reverses during a recession (UNRATE < 2% at the same time).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent when labor market is strong (UNRATE > 3.5%).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase of more than 0.4 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered months, or the effect is reversed during periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 6%).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% over three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which depresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect disappears when demand proxies (GDPC1, RSAFS) are rising.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in FEDFUNDS and a fall in CPIAUCSL (inflation) below 2% over two months signals a successful disinflationary tightening, which boosts risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL < 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent when unemployment is rising sharply (UNRATE > 3.5%).

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month indicates a broad-based demand recovery, which boosts earnings and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > +1% AND HOUST > +1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent when inflation is accelerating (CPIAUCSL YoY > 4%).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of at least 50,000 jobs over three consecutive months signals robust labor market strength, which supports consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses when wage growth (not measured here) is stagnant or falling.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 2% over four consecutive months indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue and profit forecasts, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent when overall GDP growth (GDPC1) is accelerating.
